query: What visit-note signals suggest high urgency?

per_column.name: acute_symptom_timeline
per_column.rationale: Symptom onset speed (minutes-to-hours vs. days) is an antecedent clinical signal derivable from the presenting complaint. It plausibly precedes and predicts urgency without restating it or requiring outcome knowledge.

per_column.name: urgent_diagnostic_or_intervention_trigger
per_column.rationale: Categories like critical lab findings, urgent imaging, protocol/alert activation, and transfer to higher acuity are near-synonymous with the visit being urgent, and are determined during/after the urgency assessment. This effectively encodes the outcome rather than predicting it.

per_column.name: treatment_intensity_or_escalation
per_column.rationale: Treatment intensity (ICU admission, emergent IV meds, surgery, escalation) is a downstream response to urgency, knowable only after the clinical decision. Using it to predict urgency is post-outcome leakage, not an independent predictor.

per_column.name: department_disposition
per_column.rationale: Values bake the urgency label directly into the category (e.g., 'cardiology_with_acute_issue', 'general_practice_urgent', 'dermatology_routine'). This is a restatement of urgency conditioned on department rather than an outside predictor, and partly derives from the existing 'department' column.

judge.rationale: Only one column (acute_symptom_timeline) is a legitimate outside predictor of urgency. The other three encode diagnostic triggers, treatment escalation, and urgency-labeled dispositions that are downstream consequences of or synonymous with urgency, constituting leakage/restatement. As a set the added columns would inflate any model's apparent performance while offering little genuine pre-outcome predictive leverage; the timeline feature provides modest real signal.
